blocks.raw:
<Tip>
**Memory aid:** "E-W Orientation Rule" — In tropical Philippines, orient buildings with long axis E-W (east-west). This minimizes harsh E and W sun, maximizes gentle N-S sun. Place primary views and living spaces on N or S facades. This is ERR-DSGN-035 territory—incorrect orientation is a common exam error.
</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["ERR-DSGN-035: Orienting buildings with long axis N-S instead of E-W in tropical Philippines; always prioritize E-W orientation for energy efficiency.","Misinterpreting contour lines as individual building levels rather than topographic data; contours show existing grades and slopes, not proposed floor levels.","Calculating slope percentage incorrectly (using vertical only, or forgetting to convert percentage); always use slope % = (rise÷run)×100.","Placing noise-sensitive spaces (bedrooms, offices) near noise sources (streets, highways) without considering acoustic design or buffers.","Ignoring utility locations and easements; utilities require clear access and cannot be built over.","Failing to account for seasonal wind changes (NE in winter, SW in monsoon) in ventilation and facade design.","Underestimating tree preservation value; existing large trees provide shade, stormwater absorption, and cost savings.","Not analyzing view opportunities and sight lines; overlooking chances to frame desirable views or block undesirable ones.","Assuming all sloping sites are unsuitable for building; slopes 0–15% are buildable and often provide design opportunities.","Omitting flood risk analysis in low-lying or coastal areas; critical for site safety and code compliance."]} />
